name: shadcn/ui Registry & Skill CLI
description: The highest-rated open-source UI component registry on GitHub. Copies accessible Radix UI and Tailwind CSS primitives directly into your project source tree.
author: shadcn
installCommand: npx shadcn@latest init && npx shadcn@latest add button dialog
readme:
# shadcn/ui Registry & Skill CLI (`shadcn-ui/ui`)

Ranked among the **most-starred developer UI projects on GitHub** (`108,500+` stars), **shadcn/ui** distributes open-code, WAI-ARIA compliant component primitives via a zero-lock-in JSON registry specification.

> **Registry Architecture:** Instead of installing opaque npm wrapper packages, the `shadcn` CLI resolves component dependencies from `registry.json` and writes editable TypeScript + Tailwind CSS source directly into your repository.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Initialize your project configuration (components.json)
npx shadcn@latest init

# Add individual components or custom GitHub registry URLs
npx shadcn@latest add button dialog dropdown-menu table
```

## CLI Commands & Flags

| Command | Flag | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `init` | `--defaults` | Initializes `components.json` and Tailwind CSS variables |
| `add [component]` | `--overwrite` | Downloads and writes selected component source files |
| `diff [component]` | `--yes` | Inspects upstream registry updates against local edits |
| `build` | `--output` | Compiles a custom static `registry.json` for GitHub Pages |

name: GitHub CLI & Extension Runtime
description: GitHub's official command-line tool and extension hub for managing pull requests, Actions workflow runs, releases, and interactive terminal dashboards.
author: cli
readme:
# GitHub CLI & Extension Runtime (`cli/cli`)

`gh` is **GitHub on the command line** (`39,100+` GitHub stars). It brings pull requests, issues, GitHub Actions workflow runs, and a rich community extension ecosystem directly to your terminal.

> **Extension Architecture:** Any GitHub repository prefixed with `gh-` containing an executable script can be installed as a native `gh` subcommand.

## Install Top Community Extensions

```bash
# Install the #1 rated terminal dashboard extension for PRs and Issues
gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash

# Search all available extensions across GitHub
gh extension search

# Inspect live GitHub Actions workflow runs
gh run watch
```

## Essential Commands

| Command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `gh pr create --fill` | Opens a Pull Request populated from commit history |
| `gh pr checkout <number>` | Fetches and checks out a contributor PR branch locally |
| `gh run list --limit 10` | Displays recent GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline statuses |
| `gh release create v1.0.0` | Publishes a tagged GitHub Release with binary assets |

name: GitHub Actions Checkout v4
description: The #1 most-used GitHub Action across all repositories worldwide. Checks out your Git repository onto CI/CD runners with shallow fetch and submodule support.
author: actions
readme:
# GitHub Actions Checkout (`actions/checkout@v4`)

Used in **over 95% of all GitHub Actions workflows globally**, `actions/checkout` is the foundational CI/CD building block on GitHub (`6,450+` stars, millions of dependent repositories).

> **Performance by Default:** Fetches only a single commit (`fetch-depth: 1`) by default to minimize clone latency in CI pipelines.

## Workflow Usage

```yaml
steps:
  - name: Checkout Repository
    uses: actions/checkout@v4
    with:
      fetch-depth: 0
      submodules: recursive
```

## Key Inputs

| Input | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | `${{ github.repository }}` | Repository name with owner (e.g. `actions/checkout`) |
| `ref` |Triggering SHA/branch | The branch, tag, or SHA to checkout |
| `fetch-depth` | `1` | Number of commits to fetch (`0` for full history/semver tags) |
| `submodules` | `false` | Whether to checkout submodules (`true` or `recursive`) |

name: Command Palette Zero
description: Dependency-free, WAI-ARIA compliant command menu and fuzzy launcher built as a 3.8kB Custom Element for static sites and documentation hubs.
author: sarakim
readme:
# Command Palette Zero

Drop-in `<forge-cmdk>` **Web Component** with *sub-millisecond* fuzzy scoring, full keyboard navigation, and dark/light CSS custom properties.

> Built on native [Custom Elements v1](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_components/Using_custom_elements) with **zero external dependencies** and `3.8kB` brotli size.

## CDN Installation

Paste the module script tag into your `<head>`:

```html
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@forgehub/cmdk-zero@1.8.0/dist/cmdk.min.js"></script>
```

## Usage Example

```javascript
const palette = document.querySelector('forge-cmdk');

palette.setCommands([
  {
    id: 'copy-url',
    title: 'Copy Current Page URL',
    section: 'Actions',
    shortcut: 'Mod+Shift+C',
    handler: () => navigator.clipboard.writeText(location.href)
  },
  {
    id: 'toggle-theme',
    title: 'Toggle Dark / Light Appearance',
    section: 'Preferences',
    shortcut: 'Mod+J',
    handler: () => document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark')
  }
]);
```

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Context | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Cmd+K` / `Ctrl+K` | Global | Toggle command palette modal visibility |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` | Open Modal | Navigate filtered command items |
| `Enter` | Open Modal | Execute highlighted command handler |
| `Escape` | Open Modal | Dismiss palette and restore focus |

name: Release Sentinel
description: Zero-config semantic versioning, conventional commit parser, and automated GitHub release notes generator with monorepo tag isolation.
author: alexrivera
readme:
# Release Sentinel

Automated **semantic versioning** and *changelog generation* designed for zero-maintenance [GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions) pipelines.

> **Note:** Release Sentinel requires `contents: write` permission in your workflow token to tag commits and publish release assets.

## Quick Start

1. Run the interactive initializer in your repository root.
2. Commit the generated `.github/workflows/release.yml` workflow.
3. Push any [Conventional Commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org) to `main`.

```bash
npx @forgehub/release-sentinel init --workflow
```

## CLI Flags & Options

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--workflow` | `boolean` | `true` | Scaffolds the GitHub Actions YAML workflow |
| `--dry-run` | `boolean` | `false` | Computes next SemVer bump without pushing tags |
| `--changelog-file` | `string` | `CHANGELOG.md` | Output file path for generated release notes |

name: EnvVault CLI
description: Portable command-line utility that encrypts local .env files using AES-256-GCM so secrets can be safely committed to version control.
author: marcuschen
readme:
# EnvVault CLI

Commit encrypted `.env.vault` snapshots **directly to Git** and decrypt them in *CI/CD* or local environments with a single master key.

> **Security Guarantee:** Zero plaintext disk writes occur during `env-vault exec`—variables are decrypted strictly in process memory.

## One-Line Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.forgehub.dev/env-vault | sh
```

## Core Workflow

1. **Initialize Vault:** Generate a project encryption key and create `.env.vault`.
2. **Lock Secrets:** Encrypt local `.env.production` changes before committing.
3. **Execute Process:** Run your server with decrypted secrets injected into memory.

```bash
# 1. Generate a project encryption key and initialize .env.vault
env-vault init --env .env.production

# 2. Encrypt local changes into the committed .env.vault file
env-vault lock --input .env.production --output .env.vault

# 3. Execute any process with decrypted secrets injected in memory
ENV_VAULT_KEY="vlt_9f8a..." env-vault exec -- node server.js
```

name: Edge RateGuard
description: Lightweight sliding-window rate limiter and token-bucket middleware for standard Fetch API handlers, Cloudflare Workers, and Deno Deploy.
author: priyapatel
readme:
# Edge RateGuard

Standards-based **HTTP rate limiting middleware** built on the [Web Fetch API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API) `Request` and `Response` primitives with *zero Node.js-specific dependencies*.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @forgehub/edge-rate-guard
```

## Middleware Usage

```javascript
import { createRateGuard } from '@forgehub/edge-rate-guard';

const limiter = createRateGuard({
  windowMs: 60_000,
  maxRequests: 120,
  keyGenerator: (req) => req.headers.get('cf-connecting-ip') || 'anonymous',
  standardHeaders: true
});
```

## Standard Response Headers

| Header | Example Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RateLimit-Limit` | `120` | Maximum requests permitted in the sliding window |
| `RateLimit-Remaining` | `84` | Remaining requests before throttling triggers |
| `RateLimit-Reset` | `42` | Seconds until the current window resets |
| `Retry-After` | `42` | Included on `HTTP 429` responses |
